'''Reinhardt Kiehl''' (31 May 1935 – 26 January 2026) was a German mathematician.

==Early life and education==
Kiehl was born in [[Herne, North Rhine-Westphalia]] on 31 May 1935.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120617013240/http://wwwmath.uni-muenster.de/historie/kapitel7.pdf Geschichte der Mathematik Universität Münster, Kapitel 7, pdf]</ref> From 1955, he studied mathematics, physics and astronomy at the [[University of Göttingen]] and the [[University of Heidelberg]]. He received in 1965 his Ph.D. (promotion) under [[Friedrich Karl Schmidt]] at [[Heidelberg University]] with thesis ''Äquivalenzrelationen in analytischen Räumen''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=20299}}</ref>

==Career==
From 1966 to 1968, he was a research assistant and in 1968–1969 a [[docent]] at the University of Münster, where he received his habilitation in 1968. From 1969 to 1972, he was a professor ordinarius at the [[Goethe-Universität Frankfurt am Main]]. From 1972, he was a professor ordinarius at the [[University of Mannheim]] and retired in 2003 as professor emeritus.

==Research==
Kiehl's research dealt with algebraic and arithmetic geometry and non-archimedean function theory. He wrote a textbook on the [[Weil conjectures]] and [[étale cohomology]] with [[Eberhard Freitag]]. In 1970 Kiehl was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians#List of Congresses|ICM]] in Nice, France with [[Hans Grauert]],'' Kohärenzsätze für stetige und differenzierbare Familien komplexer Räume''.

==Death==
Kiehl died on 26 January 2026, at the age of 90.<ref>[https://www.uni-mannheim.de/newsroom/kondolenzbuecher/kondolenzbuch-reinhardt-kiel/ "Trauer um Prof. em. Dr. Reinhardt Kiehl"]. ''uni-mannheim.de'' (in German). Retrieved 23 February 2026.</ref>
